title: Staged schema degradation and SDK grace playbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc proposes a pragmatic, staged approach to handling structured output over our streaming Hosted API while preserving developer ergonomics for SDKs and improving resilience for flaky networks and model regressions. Goal is to allow clients to get typed, verifiable frames when possible, but gracefully degrade to compact text or partial schema when constraints (latency, bandwidth, model drift, tool outages) force a fallback.

Why this is different (short):
- Introduces the concept of schema annealing: progressively relaxing type constraints rather than single-step failover.
- Adds a lightweight contractivity score to communicate how tightly output conforms to a schema (helps SDK decide strict vs permissive parse).
- Defines specific streaming frames for resumability and tool-call choreography that are minimal to implement in mobile/edge SDKs.

Problem statement:
Teams building integrated multi-tool experiences (code-runner, DB lookup, CRM lookups) require both: low-latency partial results (streaming) and strong structure guarantees (tools need typed arguments). Today we have binary outcomes: either the model emits a typed JSON blob (brittle) or we return free text (unusable by tools). That causes UX breakage, safety workarounds in SDKs, and heavy server-side logic to attempt repair.

Goals (measurable):
- Primary: Reduce tool-invocation failures caused by malformed structured output by 40% in 90-day pilot customers.
- Improve median time-to-first-typed-frame for streaming sessions by 30% for long-tail mobile clients via staged prefetching and small handshake preambles.
- Provide an SDK surface that lets clients opt into strict parsing, staged degradation, or best-effort mode in < 5 lines of code.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full schema-evolution/compatibility system for persisted artifacts. It focuses on live streaming contract negotiation and graceful runtime degradation.
- Not addressing on-prem private control-plane deployment specifics in this first pass (will be followups).

Key concepts / vocabulary (new):
- Schema annealing: a progressive relaxation sequence of schema constraints (strict JSON -> optional-typed -> shape-only -> text). Implemented as discrete levels the server can advertise.
- Contractivity score (0..1): server-side estimate of how confidently the output matches the current schema (0=free text, 1=verified strict match). Intended to be advisory for SDKs and telemetry.
- Staged frames: compact typed frames that allow a client to decide whether to block for a full tool call or proceed with a best-effort optimistic call.

High level handshake flow (stream session):
1) Client opens streaming session: POST /v1/responses?stream=true with headers: X-Client-SDK:js/1.4.0, Accept-Schema:my-schema-v2 || any
2) Server responds with handshake frame: {type: 'handshake', session_id, supported_schema_versions: [v2, v1], suggested_anneal_sequence: ['strict','partial','shape','text'], prefetch_manifest: {...}}
3) Client chooses mode: strict | staged | greedy and sends frames: {type: 'client-config', mode: 'staged', resume_token: null}
4) Model streaming begins; server emits frames of the form: {seq, frame_type, payload, schema_version?, contractivity, resume_token?}

Frame types (minimal set):
- handshake (server->client): session metadata and anneal sequence.
- schema_anchor (server->client): declares the schema_version and a short schema hash. Used to validate following frames.
- typed_chunk (server->client): partial typed payload following declared schema. 'contractivity' field present.
- shape_hint (server->client): when typed_chunk cannot be produced, emit a lightweight shape description (keys and approximate types) instead of full schema.
- text_chunk (server->client): plain text fallback.
- tool_call_open (server->client): indicates an attempted tool call with structured args. Includes safe-resume token.
- tool_call_result (server->client): result frame for the call (typed or text).
- tombstone / truncated (server->client): indicates an intentional truncation and why (quota / latency / model-failure).
- resume_request (client->server): client can request resume using resume_token.

Example annotated payload (streamed sequence):
1) {"type":"handshake","session_id":"s-abc","suggested_anneal_sequence":["strict","partial","shape","text"]}
2) {"seq":1,"frame_type":"schema_anchor","schema_version":"my-schema-v2","schema_hash":"sha1:abc123"}
3) {"seq":2,"frame_type":"typed_chunk","payload":{"action":"search","query":"find X"},"contractivity":0.92}
4) {"seq":3,"frame_type":"tool_call_open","payload":{"tool":"search-v2","args":{"q":"X"}},"resume_token":"r-13"}
5) {"seq":4,"frame_type":"tool_call_result","payload":{"status":"ok","rows": ...},"contractivity":0.85}

Contractivity semantics: 
- >=0.9: server believes output is schema-consistent; SDKs should accept as typed.
- 0.6-0.9: partial; SDKs may attempt to coerce or call a safe-parsing helper.
- <0.6: treat as advisory; fall back to text handlers.

SDK ergonomics (JS reference):
// Very small surface additions to existing streaming client
const s = client.streamResponses({stream:true, mode:'staged', schema:'my-schema-v2'});
s.on('handshake', h => { console.log('anneal', h.suggested_anneal_sequence) });
s.on('typed_chunk', c => { if (c.contractivity > 0.9) handleTyped(c.payload); else handlePartial(c.payload); });
s.on('tool_call_open', t => { // expose a Promise-friendly shim for developers
  // SDK will auto-ack and return a ToolCall object with lazy resume
  const call = sdk.toolRunner.expose(t.payload);
  call.awaitResult().then(renderToolResult);
});

Developer ergonomics notes:
- Default SDK behavior: mode='staged' with conservative parsing: only call tool when contractivity >= 0.9 OR when developer explicitly opts-in to best-effort.
- Convenience helpers: .coerceTo(schema) and .shapeMatches(hint) to allow small, safe coercions without complex validation code in-app.
- Error surface: single event 'stream-degraded' with fields: reason, last_good_schema, resume_token. Keep it small so mobile clients can log and react simply.

Observability and instrumentation:
- Every frame emits lightweight telemetry: frame_type, contractivity, seq_lag_ms (time between seq generations), schema_version. These feed the Console dashboard per-route/model.
- New dashboards: "Anneal transitions" (counts of sessions entering strict->partial->text), "Tool-call degradation" (tool calls that arrived with contractivity < 0.6), and "Resume churn" (resume_request frequency and failures).
- Alerting: rate of tool-call failures (by model and schema) > 5% over 1hr -> page oncall SRE.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): 10% of internal dev tenants; server emits contractivity and handshake only. SDKs opt-in via feature flag. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (pilot): 3 external beta customers; enable staged mode and tool_call_open frames. Add basic Console tiles. (4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (wider): gradual ramp to 25% of Hosted API traffic; add migration guidance and client-side helpers. (6 weeks)

Operational considerations:
- Backwards compatibility: if client doesn't speak handshake frames, server falls back to current streaming text-only behavior.
- Storage & bandwidth: typed_chunk frames are usually smaller than full JSON blobs because server can emit sparse partials; however we must account for schema_anchor duplication. We will compress anchors (anchor frequency throttle).
- Security: tool_call_open frames must be audited; we will add unique call IDs and require server-side audit logs for enterprise tenants.

Implementation notes for serving-runtime team:
- New minimal protocol layer in the streaming edge: handshake serializer, compact framed stream. Keep frame decoder in the runtime to avoid per-request CPU.
- Kernel: attach per-seq contractivity calculation based on model token probabilities + schema validator pass. This is best-effort and must not block streaming tail latency (circuit-breaker if validation > 10ms).

Open questions and tradeoffs (to resolve in design review):
- How to compute contractivity efficiently for very large schemas? Proposal: sample-based validation (randomly validate up to N leaves) and combine with token-prob signoffs from the model.
- Do we want server-enforced tool-call gating when contractivity < threshold, or keep default optimistic and let SDK choose? (safety vs UX).
- Resume token lifecycle: how long keep resume tokens for clients with offline periods? 24h? 7 days? Needs policy decision and quotas.

Sample checklist for SDK teams (implementation):
- [ ] Add handshake parser and 'mode' selection API.
- [ ] Implement Contractivity thresholds and make helper coerceTo(schema) available.
- [ ] Expose tool-call shim that returns a small tool handle to app code.
- [ ] Surface 'stream-degraded' telemetry with 3 fields.

Success metrics after 90 days:
- Tool-invocation failure rate down by 40% for pilot customers.
- Mean Time To Typed-Chunk (first typed_chunk seq) reduced by 30% across mobile SDKs.
- 80% of SDK users find default staged mode acceptable in a short feedback survey.

Owners & next steps:
- Proposal owner: Asha Mehta (product)
- Runtime design: Evan Park (serving-runtime)
- SDK API spec: Jordan Carter (developer-experience)
- Console instrumentation: Lina Gómez (observability)
- Action: schedule architecture sync (ASAP), add RFC to GH (linked artifact), and prototype handshake frame in edge canary.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
This is intentionally lightweight—aim is to get something deployable and iterative. The novelty is in giving SDKs an explicit signal (contractivity + anneal sequence) so they can make simple deterministic choices rather than brittle heuristics. Expect followups on schema evolution, on-prem considerations, and enterprise policy for resume token retention.

Unresolved items to discuss on the sync:
- Default thresholds (0.9 / 0.6) — validate with a small eval set.
- Whether shape_hint should be binary (present/absent) or carry frequency counts for ambiguous fields.
- UX for developer-flow when tool-call_open is emitted but a tool provider returns 5xx. Should we auto-retry with shape-only fallback?

End of draft.
